contract.label: Select
contract.summary: Choose one value from a list. A Root holds the value and wraps a Trigger plus a portalled, positioned Content of Items.
contract.purpose: Choose one value from a known set. The popup is portaled to the app root and matches the trigger width, so options line up under the value they replace.
useWhen: One value is chosen from a set too long for a `tabs` strip, or from one that grows.
A recurring job needs a control — a series selector, a date range — and then the same `select` appears wherever that job does.
dontUseWhen: The set is small and fixed and the choice switches panels — that is `tabs`.
The user needs to type or search — that is `combobox`.
The list holds actions rather than values — that is a `dropdown-menu`, which shrink-wraps instead of matching the trigger.

parts.name: Select
parts.description: Root. Owns the value state and wraps the trigger and content.

parts.name: SelectContent
parts.description: The popup listbox — portalled, positioned below the trigger.

parts.name: SelectGroup
parts.description: Wraps related items. Required around a SelectLabel.

parts.name: SelectItem
parts.description: A selectable option; shows a check when selected.

parts.name: SelectLabel
parts.description: A non-interactive heading for a group. Must be inside SelectGroup.

parts.name: SelectScrollDownButton
parts.description: Scroll-down affordance shown when the list overflows.

parts.name: SelectScrollUpButton
parts.description: Scroll-up affordance shown when the list overflows.

parts.name: SelectSeparator
parts.description: A thin divider between groups or items.

parts.name: SelectTrigger
parts.description: The button that opens the listbox and shows the current value.

parts.name: SelectValue
parts.description: Renders the selected item's label, or the placeholder when empty.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height — default (2rem) or sm (1.75rem). Match the other controls in the same toolbar.

props.name: surface
props.description: What the trigger sits on — default inside a card, sheet, dialog or table row, where it rests clear so the surface shows through; page straight on the shell's muted content area, where it rests and hovers like an outline Button so a filter row reads as one surface.

requires: A `SelectValue` in the trigger, so the current value is readable without opening the list.
Portalling left on, so no `overflow` ancestor can clip the popup.
forbids: A checkmark on the selected option in a single-select. The trigger value and the option highlight already say it; a check belongs only to multi-select.
Pinning a side that lets the popup run off-screen — the positioner flips and shifts by default.
Stretching or shrinking the list away from the trigger width.
Re-tinting the resting surface with a `bg-*` class so the field reads on the page body — set `surface="page"`, which is the outline Button's face in both themes.
rules: **No checkmark on the selected option** in a single-select — the trigger value plus the option highlight already say it. A check belongs only in multi-select.
The list matches the trigger width so options line up under the shown value.

**Pick the surface by what is underneath.** A trigger placed straight on the shell's `muted` content area — a filter row, a page-size select — takes `surface="page"`, which rests and hovers like an outline Button (`outline-surface`, `outline-hover`), so the row reads as one surface. Inside a `card`, `sheet`, `dialog` or table row it keeps `default`.

behavior.error: `aria-invalid` on the trigger renders the destructive border and ring, exactly as on `input`.

requirements: The trigger is labelled — by a `field` label or an `aria-label`.

examples: `<SelectTrigger size="sm" surface="page"><SelectValue placeholder="All sites" /></SelectTrigger>` in a filter row on the page body.
antiPatterns: Adding a tick to the chosen item because a design tool drew one.
A `select` for a job that a segmented control handles on another screen.

A field on the muted page body given `bg-background`, `bg-card` or `bg-white` instead of `surface="page"` — in dark mode `background` is darker than `card`, so the field sinks below the cards beside it.
